messages:
robin_oncall: incident-bot fired paging rule gpu_memory_pressure_p95 for pool-gamma - multiple CUDA alloc failures observed :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-8237 created and notified oncall schedule (ack deadline 15m)
robin_oncall: acked PD-8237, starting triage. seeing repeated 'CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY' in /var/log/inference/serving.log across 4 hosts in pool-gamma
maya_sre: which model/serving-config? any recent rollouts?
robin_oncall: it's the nightly rollout for llama-7b-quant which started ~10m before pages. config: batch_size=8, kvcache_prefetch=on, seq_len_target=1024. attaching snippet:
```
# recent deploy
model: redwood/llama-7b-quant-v2
batching:
  max_batch_size: 8
  timeout_ms: 12
kvcache:
  enabled: true
  prefetch: aggressive
```
james_infra: oof, prefetch aggressive + 7b quant can push nvmem. logs show rapid kv cache growth and then cuda oom at alloc ~ 3.3GB chunks.
robin_oncall: stacktrace excerpt: "cudart: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (error 2)" repeated. fallback policy attempted to reroute but routing queue is saturated.
maya_sre: toggling prefetch off on pool-gamma might free headroom. can you run the live config patch?
james_infra: running: `kubectl -n inference patch cm pool-gamma-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"kvcache_prefetch":"off"}}'`
robin_oncall: patch applied, restarting 2 workers on host-a and host-c with graceful drain: `svc restart worker --host host-a --grace 30s`
incident-bot: autoscaler observed evictions and started cache-evict-shedder on pool-gamma (policy: drop_kvcache_least_recent=1.0)
ella_custsuccess: any customer impact? seeing error spikes on customer-prod org: increased 500 responses for /v1/generate
robin_oncall: initial impact: 12% of requests hitting pool-gamma got 5xx, latency p95 spiked from 180ms -> 1.2s. routing fallback served lower-capacity model for some requests which increased tail. notifying customers with affected routes.
maya_sre: workers on host-a/c back up with prefetch disabled. memory graphs show used GPU mem dropped ~1.6GB per host. still seeing oom on host-b and host-d, investigating thermal/noise.
james_infra: host-b shows fragmentation: many small cuda allocations, GPU free reported ~400MB but alloc for contiguous chunk fails. trying `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset` not allowed in prod. plan B: move some pods off host-b to host-e (lower utilization).
robin_oncall: initiating pod eviction on host-b: `kubectl drain host-b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`
pagerduty-bot: PD-8237 acknowledged by robin_oncall at 3963210002 (duration 00:00:02). escalated to maya_sre at 3963210045 per escalation policy.
maya_sre: escalated. on it. shifting traffic: applying route rule to move 25% traffic off pool-gamma to pool-beta: `redwoodctl route set traffic --from pool-gamma --to pool-beta --percent 25`
ella_custsuccess: posting interim status to customers: "We're investigating increased errors for some requests; mitigation in progress. We'll post another update in 30 minutes."
james_infra: pod eviction completed on host-b, container restarted on host-e. host-b GPU health still flaky; marking host-b cordoned for deeper postmortem.
robin_oncall: can we increase fallback model capacity for critical customers temporarily?
maya_sre: yes, bumping reserved-capacity for beta to handle more: `redwood capacity commit --pool pool-beta --add 3` (takes ~60s to warm).
incident-bot: automatic diagnostic snapshot uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/PD-8237/3963210000-diagnostics.tar.gz
robin_oncall: monitoring error rate and latency. error rate trending down to 3% and p95 back to 310ms after routing + prefetch toggle.
ella_custsuccess: updated customers: "Mitigation applied; errors reduced but some requests may still see degraded latency. Follow-up report will be shared."
maya_sre: leaving temporary mitigations in place until 3963213600 (approx 1 hour) and will schedule rollback when safe. recording playbook steps and annotating runbook.
robin_oncall: marking incident as mitigated for now. leaving PD incident open for postmortem. next: deep postmortem to cover root cause (kv prefetch policy + quant interaction + fragmentation) and add automated guardrail to disable aggressive prefetch when free_gpu_mem < 4GB.
james_infra: cordon host-b, file for hardware check. tagging host-b for kernel/drivers triage.
robin_oncall: thanks all. closing the live thread. :white_check_mark:
